Hi  [~accountid:5ff58eb39edf2800758cbb77] 

After reviewing the T&Cs, please see a summary of the main terms and my comments below in red: 

*Payment policy* 

A 50% deposit of agreed sponsorship items will be invoiced at the signature of the contract. The remaining 50% will be charged and to be paid no later than 3 months before the congress. If the contract is signed *after the 1st June 2022,* *the total amount must be paid by credit card* upon receipt of the invoice. Please note that a 2.5% fee will apply. 

{color:#bf2600}BL: Considering that this contract will be signed after 1{color}{color:#bf2600}^st^{color}{color:#bf2600} June, Bolt will be obliged to pay by credit card in accordance with the clause mentioned above. Could you please confirm with the accounting department whether we are in a position to pay by credit card? {color}

*General conditions* 

All activities organized by Bot involving participants in the meeting must be approved by EPA. Distribution of drinks and meals must be in compliance with rules of the meeting venue.  

*Irregular activities* 

All gift items with the exception of plastic bags, pens, pencils, luggage labels, pocket calendars and the exhibitor's product must be sent for approval to the EPA three (3) weeks prior to the opening of the exhibition. All exhibitors distributing approved "stickers" may not place the "stickers" on attendees badges. 

Taking photographs (including cell phone cameras), videotaping, or examining another sponsor's equipment or exhibit without that sponsor's permission is prohibited. 

*Subletting and assignment* 

Bolt may not assign, sublet or apportion its space to or with another business entity or individual.  

*Works* 

Booth construction plans and layout arrangements for any booth spaces, or involving other construction features, must be submitted for approval at least sixty (60) days prior to the opening of the exposition. 

*Changes to the T&Cs* 

EPA has the sole and exclusive right to make changes, amendments and additions to Sponsor guidelines stated in the T&Cs and subsequent communications. The general terms and conditions, as amended, shall govern the actions of all sponsors. Interpretation of the sponsor general terms and conditions and operational rules shall rest solely with EPA, and the decisions of EPA shall be final. EPA may require sponsors to make such alterations to their displays as it deems necessary to the proper conduct of the exhibition. Failure to comply may result in immediate expulsion from the exhibition or the payment of reimbursement and compensation to EPA by the sponsor for all expenses related to the alteration of a booth/ display. 

*Liability* 

Neither EPA, nor its sponsors, members, officers, representatives, agents or employees, will be liable for any injury, theft, loss or damage that may occur to the exhibits.  

In the event that said premises are destroyed by fire, climatic elements or by any other cause, or by government intervention or regulation, military activity, strikes or any other circumstances which make it impossible for 20th European Parking Association Congress & Exhibition to take place, the contract shall terminate and the Bolt shall waive any claim for damages or compensation except the pro rata return of the amount paid for space, after deduction of actual expenses incurred in connection with 20th European Parking Association Congress & Exhibition. Companies are required to make their own arrangements with respect to insurance and organization of their booth. 

------- 

{color:#bf2600}BL: Please note that there is no an early termination clause (i.e. a clause that allows us to terminate the contract at any time without reason) which is always recommended. However, considering the low value of the contract and the short duration, I do not consider it to be a red flag. {color}

 

Should you have any further questions, please do let me know. 



Thank you.

Export with kibana in-built function is inconsistent for some reason (exports less than selected search window) and also requires increases of max export size and timeouts on kibana size [https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/kibana/current/reporting-settings-kb.html#reporting-csv-settings|https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/kibana/current/reporting-settings-kb.html#reporting-csv-settings|smart-link] 



So I found more predictable, flexible and easier to use external project to do this [https://github.com/fabiopipitone/elasticsearch-tocsv|https://github.com/fabiopipitone/elasticsearch-tocsv|smart-link] 



{noformat}pip install elasticsearch=="7.*" elasticsearch-tocsv{noformat}

And after this for prelive

{noformat}# run ssh port forwarding to access elastic
ssh -N -L 9200:localhost:9200 admin-kibana.prelive.security.boltint.net

# export from prelive for 3 month
elasticsearch_tocsv -f "@timestamp,http_host,request_uri,ssl_client_email,upstream_http_admin_email" -e admin-kibana.prelive.uri-users.0105-2807.csv -sd "2022-05-01" -ed "2022-08-01" -i "logs-admin-v2*" -t "@timestamp" -tz "UTC" -q "status:200" -em true -lbi 1d{noformat}



For live data is too big, that’s why export is done by week

{noformat}# run ssh port forwarding to access elastic
ssh -N -L 9200:localhost:9200 admin-elastic-1.internal

# change export filename and range for other weeks (each week ~3Gb and take ~30 min to finish)
elasticsearch_tocsv -f "@timestamp,http_host,request_uri,ssl_client_email,upstream_http_admin_email" -e admin-kibana.live.uri-users.1807-2907.csv -sd "2022-07-18" -ed "2022-07-29" -i "logs-admin-v2*" -t "@timestamp" -tz "UTC" -q "status:200" -em true -lbi 1d --process_number 4{noformat}

Hey,

_If we are essentially refunding the cancellation fee to the user, why is it needed to issue the refund to Bolt balance, and not to the user's bank account? —_ this is because the fee was charged *correctly*, so there’s no need to give the money back to the user. Instead, we may compensate them as a gesture of goodwill (if it was their first trip), and kind of keep the money in Bolt. 

_This creates, in my view, a discrepancy with automation that goes directly to the user's bank account. —_ I think that if the automation is applied, the user won’t get in touch with us anyway, and the ones that do, didn’t receive the automation. So I don’t think there’s any discrepancy here, but maybe I’m misunderstanding your question, so feel free to elaborate more on that 🙂 

_Considering that users were also not able to use the service, they are more likely to request a full refund to their bank account, for this reason, so Bolt balance refunds can easily lead to longer TRT (as users have to be convinced to accept BB) and most likely negatively affect customer satisfaction (as they will be forced to use our service to "receive" the refund). —_ can you please provide some data about it? I get your point, but I think this can be assumed with all Bolt Balance refunds: most likely, the user wants to get the money back if they were dissatisfied, but regardless of this, we should still stick to Bolt Balance whenever possible. 

_The second thing I wanted to clarify is whether we can only make an exception in cases where it is the user's first order at all or the first order with a pickup issue? If a rider has not had any issues with pickup previously, it does not passively add to their ability to deal with pickup issues in the future. —_ I would really not want to encourage everyone to start refunding all cancellation fee reports, but yes, I think there can always be exceptions. The guidelines say that we may refund if it was the first trip, but if you really feel that the compensation is justified even if the rider has had previous trips, you can compensate. I’d just take it case-by-case and not start refunding without a valid reason (if the fee was charged correctly).

The first report looks at long term leave of absence (maternity, etc.). If the report is empty you will not receive it (chances are that this will be populated rarely)

The second report will return the time off entries for Delivery Sales team. You have the team, name, and time off date. 

To know:

* depending on the country and time off plan set-up, it can be either in days or in hours, this is captured in the report (e.g. 1 day, 8 hours)
* corrections show up in the report too. Not ideal, but if I request a day for 29 July and then I requests to cancel it, in the report you will see 2 lines for me; 1 for the request, and another one with “-1” for the correction

h3. Technical thoughts

Mostly those logs will be interesting after migration failed for some reason which is not clear from the error messages. This means that we’d like to fetch logs after migration has finished (with failure), and maybe even after the pipeline has finished.

It’s not guaranteed that we will keep gh-ost logs forever (most probably not), so we can add an alternative response in case we can’t find logs on agent.

To identify which logs to fetch, we can send pipeline ID, cluster and runtime schema name in request to Supervisor, and it should be able to uniquely identify a migration. Then it can use the migration ID to ask Agent, and Agent can find logs by migration ID due to the file naming convention.

Another detail is that Supervisor needs to know which Agent to ask for logs. After the migration there could be a master switch, or instance could be recycled. transitions to signup.details.step2 (which has trackPageRenderedEvent) saveModelAndGoToNextStep(model, 2)

hi [~accountid:62275121c88f10006831a6f6], the answer to your question is very complex and it depends on many factors.

If Bolt Market does not allow their employees to use a break, there are a few consequences, 

First of all, that can trigger an inspection, and Bolt Services HR d.o.o. may face fines up to HRK 100.000,00 / approx. EUR 13.333,00 in case of every breach. 

Additionally,  the responsible person in the company may be fined in the amount up to HRK 10.000,00.  

Furthermore, employees that are working longer hours have a right to a higher salary for their overtime (the percentage by which it is increased is prescribed in the employment contract, but usually is 50% higher)

Also,  depending on the situation, a disgruntled employee could potentially terminate the employment agreement by extraordinary dismissal and could claim damages from the employer.

This matter has now been resolved. 

The key issues here were the following:

# Only the first page of the bill for these business rates were paid, this meant that we fell overdue on payments for the business rates on our car parks at the Chiswick Hub for all other car spaces we were responsible for.

# Due to a delay in confirmation of payments from both finance and property, we were unable to attend the magistrates court date to defend Bolt. 
# Given we missed the court date, this matter was referred to the debt collection agency CDER. Thankfully, they were receptive to us settling this before taking further action and (potentially impacting our credit rating). Finance were able to pay the outstanding debts + penalties as a result of the delay. This was delayed slightly as finance had paid an additional amount of fees but we needed additional proof on allocated invoices from the council once CDER notified us we still hadn't paid everything (£47K still missing - see attachment from CDER). 
# Eventually everything was paid and finance gave us the heads up some of these business rates payments are for the year ahead in 2022>2023, this is likely due to our delay on payments for the last 2 years. Amida will now liaise with the Chiswick agents to get a rebate on some of the car park rates we’ve already paid for which we are no longer using and therefore entitled to a rebate. 
# We now have the attached proof from CDER and my email to the council confirming all debts are paid. Once I received a response back from the council this will be filed as well and hopefully they agree to an undertaking not to take further action, aligned with the CDER. 

Any questions do reach out. 

Many thanks,

Clarissa

Hi [~accountid:5b1146f84bec0e53fdb543f5], 

After reviewing your query, my opinion is that there are a lot of risks regarding this plan. 

First of all, if we start punishing and fining couriers, there is a reclassification risk since we start controlling them. 

Secondly, in order for Bolt to have a right to fine couriers, we would need to have an agreement with couriers that mentions this right. 

Please note that our current T&Cs do not give Bolt any right to fine couriers, so at the moment the only way to claim any damages from couriers is to initiate a court proceeding. 

Finally, in case we do fine them without the agreement we risk couriers initiating a court proceeding against Bolt claiming the return of their earnings - in this proceeding the burden of proof would be on Bolt i.e. Bolt would need to undoubtedly prove that the courier provided a bad service (just a client’s complain would not be enough to prove it).

Best regards, 

Iva

Hey \!

Yes, I also agree that we should not compensate driver mistakes, but sometime those mistakes can actually be legit and we do not want to risk drivers starting to mislike us, because of a small fee. We have talked to numerous of drivers regarding cancellation fees, and many of them are saying that it’s very annoying when the pick up destination is inside of a area where it’s not possible to enter with a car.. so if trips get’s cancelled and they are to far away from the pick up area (I believe it’s something like 150meter) the fee will not be added. This is of course hard for us to monitor, so I dont have a clear guideline on how to solve this.

_“If the driver did not meet the predicted ETA but was well on their way to or had already arrived at the pickup point when the trip was cancelled, compensate the cancellation fee.”_

Yes, agree with this. This has also been a huge thing drivers telling us. It’s very irritating for the drivers to actually start driving towards the pickup destination, and are well on their way, and then the trip get’s cancelled, without any fee. In a competitive environment, especially during the weekend, this is very frustrating for the drivers. It can also be numerous of reasons why the ETA was not met, and the ETA does rarely match the reality, as this has been seen by us also. It can say ETA 6 min, but it’s not a chance in the world for the driver to get there in 6min. I have also seen during a trip how the ETA does not match what is stated. “Your driver is here in 5min” then 8… then 3…then 5 again and so on. If this results in the customer cancelling the trip, and the driver is well on his way.. this should be considered for compensation.

And finally, Yes - B2B trips can result in drivers have to go in the wrong direction first, before they can move towards the customer. If the driver does this, and is well on his way towards the customer, we should consider compensation.

I discussed this a bit, will add my thoughts as bullet points:

* Yes, in a way, there is a _discrepancy_ between the automation and our refund logic. However, automation is only applied once per every 30 days, and if the automation is applied, the user probably will not get in touch with us and won’t even know about the discrepancy. Even if they did, there’s nothing wrong here because if the cancellation fee is applied *correctly*, we’re not obliged to even issue any compensation. Issuing it to BB is just a gesture of goodwill and the automation is in place to reduce incoming contacts as of course some people would like to get their money back, even if everything was charged correctly and they were notified about it.
* Re Bolt Balance refund negatively impacting some support KPIs: as I mentioned previously too, it can happen with all Bolt Balance refund cases because there will always be users who will want their money back. However, we should still stick to Bolt Balance whenever possible (and justified). In situations where users start demanding for a full refund, I think we should use our soft skills and also know when to end the conversation. Just because users are demanding something doesn’t mean we should give it to them. There are always exceptions and situations where you feel a full refund would be justified, so please feel free to use full refunds in those exceptions. 
** Re the data: I was thinking about it and currently, the only way we could actually measure this would be conducting a test: for some period of time, we offer a full refund in those cases and for some period of time, we follow the current process. However, we should also keep in mind that Bolt Balance was created for that purpose (to offer compensation without fully refunding the order), so unfortunately, I don’t see any benefits of that test. Again, it all comes down to using soft skills when users are demanding something and a full refund is clearly not justified. If that happens, we should try to explain that we’ve done everything we can and avoid going back-and-forth with the customer for several replies.

As the process will not be changed, I will close the ticket, but if you have any additional questions, let me know here.

_Possible solutions include_
## Adding new columns of row numbers with descending value, either in product level or ETL level, to identify last ticket (assuming last ticket is the true reason of churning). These new columns will act as flag, for example a {{ticket_created_sequence}} with value = 1 is the last ticket created by that user, value = 2 is the ticket before the last ticket. etc. We can create several columns with different sequences, for example {{ticket_resolved_sequence}}(sequence based on resolution timestamp), {{ticket_responded_sequence}}(sequence based on response from CS agent timestamp), etc. Depending on the context, these flag could be used to filter out rows that is outside of our interest.

Hi team,

Have you any update?

*Issues*

In general, the most important debate in determining business company debt real source is in defining the label: whether it’s company-level or transaction-level. Some debt source is company-level, for example fraudulent company and credit limit issues. However, some other is also invoice-level or transaction-level, such as incorrect payment details, incorrect company details, postpaid with CC autodebit, and fraudulent transactions. The fraudulent actor also may come from employees instead of the business company.

To resolve these issues, careful consideration must be made when setting up the definition.

*Business Debt Life Cycle*

Business companies have credit limit, which they can use until the credit limit is reached. At the beginning of each month, they receive a monthly invoice with owed amount. They can pay, or they can wait until the credit limit is reached. Currently I’m not sure about the blocking mechanism, but in general, a company will be blocked if: (a) they reach the credit limit, or (b) last N months of invoices are unpaid, determined by the account manager.

Before they receive an invoice, their employee can use the credit to use Bolt’s services. The employees are a different entity, and financially, their behavior shouldn’t affect the company’s debt to Bolt. After each service is used, the company got charged for the “claim”, when the company will get charged immediately using CC if they use CC invoicing type. For postpaid companies, the claim will be recorded as negative entry in their balance, and at the end of the month Bolt will bill the companies. For postpaid companies with CC payment option, the companies will be charged automatically every 3 days ([https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/3388375589/Credit+Card+Postpay|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/3388375589/Credit+Card+Postpay|smart-link]). 

Based on this life cycle, there is three payment points:

# After every claim, for CC companies
# Every 3 days, automatically charged to CC for postpaid companies with CC payment option activated
# Anytime, after they receive monthly invoice. Usually paid by bank transfers.

So, how do we determine source of debt?

----

*Transaction level (claim-level) labelling*

We can attribute payment status to each claim. For CC companies, we can attach the CC charge to each claim, for example how many payment attempt, what are the reason for failure, and other reason. We can also mark the transaction as paid if the future payment settle the debt, for example the debt is paid off by the cron job (_2nd payment point_) or bank transfer (_3rd payment point_).

The debt from a transaction will be carried on to the charge from the next transaction. We can also link payment attempt from the future to the previous claims. By doing this, we can see the payment failure from earliest attempts and latest attempts, getting better visibility on the cause of the problem.

Beside problems from payment, we can also attach other attributes based on the order itself, such as fraudulent order, refunded order, fraudulent employee, etc.

_Possible labels for transaction level: earliest reason of failure (CC), latest reason of failure (CC), # of payment attempts both from claim or from cron, order attributes from the user. The link between transaction and the attributes can be made as one-to-one (transaction and summary of attributes), or one-to-many (transaction and list of future payment attempts)._ 

_Potential opportunities:_

* Reducing the charged amount if the last charged amount caused by insufficient fund, so instead of charging large amount at once we can try implement gradual charges.
** Risk assessment: legal risk?
** Impact assessment: does past insufficient fund cause payment failure in the future, especially if the debt is getting bigger? What is the increment of the debt amount, is it big? Does bigger charge lead to payment issues from the bank (e.g. fraud-related payment abortion)
* Bill CC companies using regular autodebit, such as postpaid companies
** Check whether this setup is already operating right now
* Possibility to add multiple CC/debit cards: alternative source of fund
** Risk assessment: legal risk
** Impact assessment: will companies do this?
* Review CC authentication steps
** Required fields: first name, last name, card number, security code, expiration date, etc
** Cross border payment possibility

*Autodebit level labelling*

This is not a dimension considered in the debt data model, but an attribute to the transaction level label. 

*Bank transfer labelling*

This is very tricky as the amount of failed bank transfer are not recorded in the balance history, but we could draw some conclusions from failed payment attempts, such as wrong reference number, or different bank account source. It it not in billing team’s scope to analyze unmatched payment and link it to each business companies, and because the payment never reach our system, we can’t label a transaction based on failed bank transfer attempts. 

What we could do is match past transactions, that is still unpaid at the moment of bank transfer, match them based on other attributes such as country, amount, reference, and other factors, and put ML-based probability score to each “matching” payments. 

Possible scoring methods:

* Payment duration, referenced to average & variance of payment duration in the same market.
** _Example: on average, it needs 15 days to pay the debt in that market, with standard deviation of 7 days. If the payment are made closer to the average, and with careful consideration of the standard deviation, the score will be bigger._
* Payment amount
** _Example: debt amount before the payment → 500 eur, payment 495 eur. Only 5 eur difference or 1%, so payment score is 99%._ 
* Payment source
** _Example: source score will show several score based on payment country source, for example 100% if the payment made from the same economic zone, 50% if the payment made by neighboring economic zone, and 0% if the payment made from a far country_

_Finally: compute weighted average for the final score, and set a threshold. If threshold exceeds X%, then that unmatched payment can be attributed to the unpaid transaction._

then we also need to assess whether the unmatched payments are already refunded or not, attempt to refund unmatched payment in our system, or do some effort to match them manually. 

We could add this failed payment as additional attribute to transaction level label, only if the bank transfer happen after the last CC charge and happen not long after the last claim. 

*Other events*

# CS ticket about wrong company details → may be a friction that hinder debt collection
## Challenge: find user_id for email user_type
# Other CS tickets → worth checking
## Challenge: find user_id for email user_type
# Escalation through service desk → issues raised by account managers

*Company level labelling*

Label attributed to each company, such as

* deactivation reason: fraud, churn, and other reason

----

*Final data model*

Similar to other {{billing_debt_{entity}}} views, we will build a {{billing_debt_business}} that show a transaction level debt dynamics. Beside the main table, we also need to build a peripheral table {{billing_debt_business_payment_attempts}} that display all information related to payment attempts, CS ticket, and unmatched bank transfer. We also need to create additional table to store CS & SD tickets, e.g. {{billing_debt_business_tickets}}.

----

*Design of* {{billing_debt_business}} *schema*

business_company_id - integer
id - primary key of the table
date - transaction created date
currency - string
amount - float
transaction_type - string, categorical (claim, topup, bank_transfer, etc etc)
current_balance - running current balance
surplus_current_balance - running current balance of positive amounts
deficit_current_balance - running current balance of negative amounts
latest_current_balance - final amount of current balance (start-to-end)
latest_surplus_current_balance - final amount of surplus current balance (start-to-end)
latest_deficit_current_balance - final amount of deficit current balance (start-to-end)
is_due - boolean. 1 if amount is negative (marker of negative balance)
amount_due - (-1 * amount) if is_due is true
amount_paid - amount paid, value ranges from \[0,1]*amount_due, based on FIFO approach
paid_ratio - ratio of amount paid to amount due
is_fully_paid - boolean, true if paid_ratio is 1
payment_date - date when the debt from that transaction is settled
debt_age - date diff between {{date}} and {{coalesce(payment_date, current_date)}}
count_payment_attempt - future payment attempts, CC from claim + autodebit
count_payment_attempt_claim - future payment attempts, CC from claim
count_payment_attempt_autodebit - future payment attempts, CC from autodebit
count_payment_bank_transfer - future payment attempts from bank transfer. accuracy is lower
count_cs_ticket - cs ticket raised after the transaction and before the debt is settled
count_sd_escalation - sd escalation after the transaction and before the debt is settled
first_failed_payment_attempt_method - CC/autodebit/transfer, string
last_failed_payment_attempt_method - CC/autodebit/transfer, string
last_successful_payment_attempt_method - CC/autodebit/transfer, string
first_failed_payment_attempt_id - integer, point to {{billing_debt_business_payment_attempts}}
last_failed_payment_attempt_id - integer, point to {{billing_debt_business_payment_attempts}}
last_successful_payment_attempt_id - integer, point to {{billing_debt_business_payment_attempts}}
first_failed_payment_attempt_reason - string
last_failed_payment_attempt_reason - string
first_ticket_id - integer, may point to beehive or service desk
last_ticket_id - integer, may point to beehive or service desk

*Design of* {{billing_debt_business_payment_attempts}} *schema*

id - integer, primary key

*Issue with Bad Debt Definition*

Bad debt is defined as unpaid debt with debt age >= 90. However, the unpaid rate of total credit transactions alway decrease, even though with lower rate as the debt age progressed. For example, in April NG’s unpaid rate is 0.76% (all of them are bad debt). However, in December 2021 the unpaid rate is only 0.43%. There is a portion of drivers that pay the debt after 90 outstanding days. This shows that the older portion of bad debt do decrease over time.

It will be very useful to have a sophisticated time to event model to predict duration until pay back for each entity, and define bad debt based on that calculation. However, it is not easily done for now, so we need to accept the definition of 90 days criteria. 

_Future plans:_

* time-to-event prediction to predict bad debt - more complex criteria, may not be very useful for accounting, but will be useful for analytics.
* fix debt age calculation, instead of from transaction date to invoice date - better visibility and validity of “debt”, as the debt is backed by invoices.

*Temporary Solution: How to Estimate Bad Debt?*

This temporary solution is limited to Looker functionality, so the prediction is not very accurate. In the future, after we have a more sophisticated bad debt prediction, this temporary solution will be dropped. The reason why a more robust solution is not possible now, because such task need more planning, research, and implementation.

This temporary solution use the average of unpaid rate during the period of bad debt (_from 5 months ago to 9 months ago_). So, for example, today (2022-08-03):

{noformat}August: 0k bad debt, 30k unpaid debt, 50% unpaid rate
July: 0k bad debt, 15k unpaid debt, 15% unpaid rate
June: 0k bad debt, 5k unpaid debt, 5% unpaid rate
May: 1k bad debt, 3k unpaid debt, 1% unpaid rate
April: 1k bad debt, 1k unpaid debt, 0.5% unpaid rate
March: 900 bad debt, 900 unpaid debt, 0.5% unpaid rate
February: 900 bad debt, 900 unpaid debt, 0.5% unpaid rate
January: 900 bad debt, 900 unpaid debt, 0.5% unpaid rate
December: 900 bad debt, 900 unpaid debt, 0.5% unpaid rate{noformat}

In the example below, bad debts in August-June are 0 because the debt age is less than 90 days. Bad debt in May is less than the total unpaid debt because the majority portion of the debt is not bad debt (less than 90 days), but there are some days which the debt age >= 90 (hence, bad debt). For April to December, as all debt have >= 90 days debt age, bad debt = unpaid debt.

Then, we calculate the {{Adjusted Average Unpaid Rate}} by average unpaid rate from December (9 months ago) to April (4 months ago, except for business where we only calculate until March or 5 months ago). In this example, the {{Adjusted Average Unpaid Rate}} is 0.5%. 

The {{Predicted Bad Debt}} is simply total credit value (paid debt + unpaid debt) in each month multiplied by 0.5%. This approach is a simplification and result in inaccurate result, especially in the earliest months and latest months, where the predicted bad debt > actual bad debt in December and vice versa in April.

*Note:*

* The predicted bad debt is calculated using actual total debt as the base of the calculation. This way, the predicted bad debt for the current month, especially during the early days of the month, will be smaller than it actually is.

Call verification has improved.
ATIs - improvement in understanding.

Calibrate on the findings weekly; review Solution Coaches. Focus on the mistakes. They review tickets together before the weekly calibration meets (including 10-25 reviewers from their side).

More specifically, best example, locations-orders-live-elastic cluster is very heavily utilizing RAM for disk caching. It can be seen during instance restart and somewhat on elasticsearch service restart, but once cache is warm it would seem that instance is idling and can be downscaled.

However, without all that free RAM, disk IO would be very high for long time and cluster would not perform as expected.


In live-delivery case, I am not sure, but we can experiment with changing JVM allocated memory.

Hi, I agree with the assessment, it is so broad that it is difficult to understand what info is required from us. As it stands, I would decline the request, but we can use parts of the following points to respond and show good faith: 

* Any disclosure of personal data from Bolt for law enforcement purposes must still comply with the UK GDPR, and in particular, a lawful basis is required at Art.6. The disclosure must be necessary and proportionate to the stated purpose.
* Bolt cannot lawfully disclose this information only having been told that the purpose concerns an "investigation". With no details having been provided, Bolt cannot undertake nor document an assessment for lawful disclosure - as required by law. The threshold of criminality is unknown, and so any test for necessity and proportionality is made impossible. 
* In the disclosure request, no link was mentioned between the data points with criminal activity, and the purpose beyond the "investigation". The potential, even inadvertent, loss of those third party's right to privacy must be warranted in these circumstances, and the use or intention of that data upon disclosure explained (at least at high level). In short, compliance with the current disclosure request conflicts with other legal obligations with which Bolt is required to comply i.e. data protection.
* Bolt has a dedicated function and support staff to manage such enquiries which are handled under the strictest of confidence. Should you wish to share the criminal activity associated with the investigation, and demonstrate (at a high level) why the loss of privacy in this instance is warranted and required to assist in that investigation, then please do let us know.

I am also looping in our RH product counsel/guru [~accountid:5fa118a781b2880078eb0e6f] for his insight and views about exclusivity deals in high-market share environment. 

Quick question to narrow our focus on this: the fleets that we want to offer preferential rates to - do they employ their drivers? 

Here is also the longer consideration/explanation from external counsel if you wish to consider it in more detail:

_As requested, we have looked into your below query on a high-level basis. Further to this we believe that the exclusivity arrangement which you have outlined in your email may be deemed to be both an anti-competitive arrangement, and/or an abuse of the dominant position, where the former is prohibited through Article 101 of the TFEU and Article 5 of the Competition Act, and the latter is prohibited through Article 102 of the TFEU and Article 9 of the Competition Act, respectively. As expressed in Article 5 of the Competition Act, any agreement between undertakings, any decision by an association of undertakings and any concerted practice between undertakings having the object or effect of restriction of competition in Malta, is prohibited._

_Although it can be argued that the company simply wishes to encourage brand loyalty, one can interpret such exclusivity incentives and/or arrangements as inducing the fleet partner to exclusively provide his services to Bolt hence, Bolt having exclusive supply of services. This, in turn would provide consumers with a lesser market choice, since the fleet partners would no longer offer their services to the public under their own name, as a ‘company that provides taxi services’ or on behalf of another undertaking through a similar arrangement, hence restricting competition in the market._

_Its object can be interpreted to be that of restricting competition as there would be less competitors in the market, potentially strengthening Bolt’s position. Furthermore, the incentivization continues to lock this agreement’s anti-competitive object in place, that of wanting the fleet to exclusively supply taxi services under the Bolt company._

_However, Article 5 of the Competition Act does come with exceptions. Article 6 of the Competition Act expresses that these agreements/arrangements will not be held to be anti-competitive if their impact in the market is minimal. This could be of the benefit for Bolt especially if the fleets that were working independently prior to the arrangement were not lead players in the market. To assess this, one must consider all relevant circumstances such as the aggregate share of all the undertakings concerned of the relevant market. Agreements between undertakings are also excluded from the prohibitions of Article 5 of the Competition Act when their beneficial effects outweigh their anti-competitive effects, however, as you may note, this may be quite subjective._

_Since Bolt is quite a dominant player in the local ride-hailing market, it may be subject to more scrutiny in its actions and is expected to develop higher standards of competitive behaviour, to compete actively, and not reduce its competition and lessen the consumer market choice. Thus, and sort of exclusivity incentives may further be interpreted to be abusing its local dominant position._

_On an EU level, agreements of a similar nature, such as loyalty rebates, have been the subject of two different approaches. They have sometimes been deemed as an objective abuse of the dominant position, concluding that these types of agreements are ‘per se prohibitions’, even without assessing whether this rebate has affected market behaviour, and, in other instances, they have been considered to only be an abuse primarily when the agreement causes a change in market behaviour. It has also been the case that some agreements could only be held not to be in breach if one is able to objectively justify the agreement. However, this has almost always been rejected from the European Courts and the Commission. Maltese cases have been in congruence with these interpretations._

_In view of the above, it is likely that the arrangements noted within your email may be deemed to be anti-competitive. In this regard, Bolt may also encourage retention of exclusivity in other, more indirect manners and one of the main ways could be implementing an incentive program without the condition of needing its Fleet Partners to remain exclusive to Bolt. These could take the form of an extra compensation based on performance, amongst any other criteria. More so, non-monetary incentives could also be used such as heightened and top-of-the-class health programs._

Hi,

1. There are no updates on the OTCs, the Ministry of Health is expecting an answer from the Pharmacies Association, who should agree with the amendments to the law to allow delivery platforms to sell OTCs. However, both MoH and the Association explained that in no way delivery bags are suitable to transport OTCs. Doc with updates here: [https://docs.google.com/document/d/19d63O-pQoNmKp2y4aa9gv9ni4s4pC3BB/edit#heading=h.1iy4mwi8oafg|https://docs.google.com/document/d/19d63O-pQoNmKp2y4aa9gv9ni4s4pC3BB/edit#heading=h.1iy4mwi8oafg|smart-link] 

2. Regarding Covid test, there is an option to directly ask the Medical Devices Authority whether we need or not authorisation to directly sell the tests. I did some research and I have the following info from the Medical Devices Authority: 

a. The distribution of medical devices for in vitro diagnosis for professional use can be carried out to other economic operators in the distribution chain, *who have an operating permit for the distribution of medical devices, in order to resell or donate the products.*

b. Regarding the *online marketing* of some medical devices intended for use by professionals, *at the moment there are no legal provisions prohibiting this practice*. As there are no regulations in this regard, the Authority cannot prohibit the sale of these products in the online system. However, the Authority recommends avoiding this way of marketing or, if this form of distribution is resorted to, it recommends that the sale of rapid tests be accompanied by a warning in accordance with the instructions for use, namely "FOR PROFESSIONAL USE ONLY". Otherwise, the economic operator may be sanctioned for misleading commercial practice.

*From the above I understand that:* 

a. Bolt Market needs an operating permit for the distribution of medical devices, if it intends to resell the covid tests;

b. No need for permits if Bolt Market does only the delivery (from one seller to client).

Please see here (google translate) the *letter we drafted for the Authority*, it will not be sent until we decide together the following steps: [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1qgHLRs8NzO2gM1-rJfRcadtAeOy8pvNe/edit|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1qgHLRs8NzO2gM1-rJfRcadtAeOy8pvNe/edit|smart-link]

Hi [~accountid:6151cf6878e5e40070fb74c2],

Please find below the external counsel’s advice:





*I.*                   +*Background*+

 

From the information provided, we understand that the Bolt Market team wants to create a marketing campaign to improve the value proposition of Bolt. To this end the team wants to communicate to Bolt customers a comparison between Bolt prices for certain products and local supermarket prices for the same products via ads, comms and app banners.

 

*II.*                +*Legal requirements to conduct comparative advertising*+

Comparative advertising, according to Portuguese law is the advertising that identifies, explicitly or implicitly, a competitor or the goods or services offered by a competitor.

As a general rule, this type of advertising is only allowed in Portugal if certain strict conditions are fulfilled (article 16 of the Portuguese Advertising Code and article 7(2)(a) of the Unfair Commercial Practice Regime).

+In Portugal, comparative advertising must:+

* Be truthful and not be misleading;
* Compare goods or services that meet the same needs or have the same objectives;
* Objectively compare one or more essential, relevant, verifiable and representative features of those goods or services, +*which may include price*+;
* Not create confusion in the market place between professionals, between the advertiser and a competitor or between the advertiser's trademarks, trade names, other distinguishing marks, goods or services and those of a competitor;
* Not disparage a competitor's trademarks, trade names, other distinguishing marks, goods, services, activities or circumstances;
* In all cases of products with designation of origin, refer to products with the same denomination;
* Not take unfair advantage of the reputation of a trademark, trade name or other distinguishing mark of a competitor or of the designation of origin of competing products;
* Not present a good or service as an imitation or reproduction of a good or service whose trademark or trade name is protected.

 

Additionally, we note that whenever the comparison makes reference to a special offer, it must clearly and unequivocally state its term or, where applicable, that such special offer is subject to the availability of products or services, when this special offer has not yet started, the starting date of the period during which the special price or any other specific condition is applicable must also be indicated.

Please note that +the burden of proving the accuracy of comparative advertising lies with the advertiser+.

Furthermore, some products and services have specific advertising rules, such as is the case with medicines, financial services, energy and a few others. Consequently, some care should be taken when dealing with the marketing of these goods and services that have specific regulators.

 

*III.*             +*Fines/consequences for non-compliance with such legal requirements*+

In the case of illicit comparative advertising or advertising that, due to its object, form or purpose, entails or may entail risks to the health, safety, rights or interests legally protected of its addressees, minors or the public, the competent authority for the application of the fines provided for in the Portuguese law, upon proposal of the entities with competence for the supervision of advertising infractions, may order precautionary measures of suspension, cessation or prohibition of that advertising, regardless of guilt or proof of loss or real damage.

The above-mentioned fines are as follows:

* From 

*1750 (euro) to 3750 (euro)* or from *3500 (euro) to 45 000 (euro),* depending on whether the offender is *a natural or legal person*.

* Negligence is always punishable.

Finally, any professional or competitor with a legitimate interest in combating misleading advertising and ensuring compliance with the provisions on comparative advertising may request the intervention of the Portuguese Directorate-General for Consumer Affairs.

It should also be noted that Portugal has a system of self-regulation in advertising matters. The self-regulation body is called Auto-Regulação Publicitária ([+https://auto-regulacaopublicitaria.pt/+|https://eur02.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fauto-regulacaopublicitaria.pt%2F&data=05%7C01%7Cvsandrade%40mlgts.pt%7C293e5e7692ee4782f3af08da76c49866%7C37dacaebcdcb4e5cbb53b1cb902cce84%7C0%7C0%7C637952883991302311%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJWIjoiMC4wLjAwMDAiLCJQIjoiV2luMzIiLCJBTiI6Ik1haWwiLCJXVCI6Mn0%3D%7C3000%7C%7C%7C&sdata=QcLGNen01Fd1lhw8qmUTlDHQHveOP7CGqtW4Kd29hLs%3D&reserved=0]).

Complaints may be filed with this entity and it will deliver very quick decisions regarding the lawfulness of advertising campaigns. The decisions are not binding to non-members but they carry a lot of weight and influence in Portugal and normally are highly publicized in the Portuguese media when the parties in question are well-known companies.

 

*IV.*             +*Any other legal considerations we must take into account.*+ 

We provide below some examples of comparative advertising that has been seen in Portugal.

Examples of comparative advertising:

# +Lidl Campaign+

 

!https://mail.google.com/mail/u/0?ui=2&ik=55261b3056&attid=0.1&permmsgid=msg-f:1740319801768294807&th=1826dba39bfa3997&view=fimg&fur=ip&sz=s0-l75-ft&attbid=ANGjdJ-PMJ7yTW2OAsMCKwUQ0bEYbdFXzbe8Xu4sh04GlRTSRLra2V1tKlw6r7zPAKeACnADaULP_xCj04tKLjUv9hylMJbQN8pIwyhL-uzlk85iVS3ysE90WlNCZz8&disp=emb|thumbnail!

Note: this comparative advertising is allowed if it is true. In this case, Lidl has even included the invoice as part of the campaign.

 

# +Intermarchê vs. Other supermarket brands+

 

!https://mail.google.com/mail/u/0?ui=2&ik=55261b3056&attid=0.2&permmsgid=msg-f:1740319801768294807&th=1826dba39bfa3997&view=fimg&fur=ip&sz=s0-l75-ft&attbid=ANGjdJ-mJO0Pv8cupzkOJmAivQ5htjfaavNFKJO9045qWqjWA-YsndTmS70Fwnmy3B-Bm2tX503h5zPS6U1P6hnNA3Ecoq3XqCYgzIV5nlkKRreyVpFlySjj0AGirYM&disp=emb|thumbnail!

Note: whenever this price comparison corresponds to the truth and deals with comparable goods and services, comparative advertising is allowed (subject to the respect of the other conditions mentioned above also).

 

*V.*                +*Conclusion*+

In short, provided that Bolt Market follows the requirements mentioned above and puts together a truthful and fair campaign, it is possible to compare prices for certain products. This has been done in the recent past by supermarket chains such as Lidl and Intermarché.

Stemming from the [EDPB guidelines|https://edpb.europa.eu/system/files/2021-11/edpb_guidelinesinterplaychapterv_article3_adopted_en.pdf] (p 14)*, such situations where an employee of a controller in the EU gets remote access to data from another country is not considered as transfers of data to third countries. 
*(_Remote access of personal data from a third country, does not qualify as a transfer of personal data)._

Therefore we don’t have a concern around international data transfers here and objections from privacy side. 

But still the remote working guidelines must be followed:

I think it would make sense to replicate how things work for the International CS Safety team, otherwise, we will end up having too many different escalation workflows. 

* The tool for countries covered by the international CS safety team has a field named *International Safety Team Review*, where 3 statutes can be selected: *Escalate, Under Review, and Review Completed*. 
* CS opens the tool for both regular and significant events. 
* CS completes the regular events themselves (complete the tool) and then escalates the significant tools to CS Safety by selecting ”Escalate”. Also, regular events that require blocking are escalated to CS Safety.

Hey

Comp&Ben has prepared salary ranges globally for all job levels in all job families. We are managing and maintaining one master file: [https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1r7M8zn6UXfxBxrbkptUBwbrjYho5_gdK-Rc2LE6xxwQ/edit#gid=1478009508|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1r7M8zn6UXfxBxrbkptUBwbrjYho5_gdK-Rc2LE6xxwQ/edit#gid=1478009508|smart-link]

This file is used by People Partners and recruitment. It is not shared with managers, because we cannot make all the ranges across all families and levels too available.

Most of these salary ranges have also been uploaded to Workday. For new ranges we either add them manually by ourselves or ask for help with mass upload (happened just once so far prior to salary review in Feb).

The problem however is that there is no clear process for sharing the ranges. The guideline we have set is that Comp&Ben is managing the master file and it is up to People Partners to figure out how their divisions get the data. Logically, the People Partner would need to define what are the needs of the managers they're supporting (who should see what) and then for example create a copy of the ranges file and share it with relevant people and remain responsible for keeping it up to date – that's one option for now but it does work in reality so well.

Our usual suggestion is that each manager can share their own job family and the levels under them (not see their own level and not levels above).

We were hoping that people tech / analytics would be able to figure out some better technical solution here. Some ideas:

# Integrated google sheets so that even though CB team is managing one file, then if we make changes they would automatically appear in other division specific files.
# Workday report which shows the manager all the ranges they need to see, being cautious of not oversharing.

Defining who are the people that should have visibility (who should see what), would still most likely be People Partner's responsibility.

Those are just some ideas, to get better picture we can discuss this further.

Main goal here is to build better technical solution for sharing the salary ranges.
More details here too: [https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C02950DQCEP/p1643548755980089|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C02950DQCEP/p1643548755980089|smart-link]

Looking forward to your feedback.
Kimberli

I reviewed added data protection clause - please see my comments in the attached doc. In essence there are 2 points that would be helpful to clarify with the supplier:

# Privacy notice- under clause VIII sec. 3, Bolt will be required to provide the data subjects whose data will be disclosed to OBI with the information about OBI being additional data controller (in other words deliver on the notification requirements on behalf of OBI). Please note that this will require additional effort from the business owner. I understand that this will be limited to employee data only, but in order to minimise organisational burden, I suggest to ask the supplier to provide their privacy notice, so there would be a ready-to-use template in place.
# Consent - in accordance with clause VIII sec. 4, Bolt will be required to collect the consent from the data subjects for transferring their data to 3rd country. Given that possible disclosure will be performed by two European entities, it is not clear why the consent would be needed in the first place. This is also not in line with our standard practice to obtain such consents, as whenever needed we are relying on other safeguards permissible under GDPR (such as SCCs).

Kind regards,

Adriana

*PT*

*I.*                   +*Background*+

 

From the information provided, we understand that the Bolt Market team wants to create a marketing campaign to improve the value proposition of Bolt. To this end the team wants to communicate to Bolt customers a comparison between Bolt prices for certain products and local supermarket prices for the same products via ads, comms and app banners.

 

*II.*                +*Legal requirements to conduct comparative advertising*+

Comparative advertising, according to Portuguese law is the advertising that identifies, explicitly or implicitly, a competitor or the goods or services offered by a competitor.

As a general rule, this type of advertising is only allowed in Portugal if certain strict conditions are fulfilled (article 16 of the Portuguese Advertising Code and article 7(2)(a) of the Unfair Commercial Practice Regime).

+In Portugal, comparative advertising must:+

* Be truthful and not be misleading;
* Compare goods or services that meet the same needs or have the same objectives;
* Objectively compare one or more essential, relevant, verifiable and representative features of those goods or services, +*which may include price*+;
* Not create confusion in the market place between professionals, between the advertiser and a competitor or between the advertiser's trademarks, trade names, other distinguishing marks, goods or services and those of a competitor;
* Not disparage a competitor's trademarks, trade names, other distinguishing marks, goods, services, activities or circumstances;
* In all cases of products with designation of origin, refer to products with the same denomination;
* Not take unfair advantage of the reputation of a trademark, trade name or other distinguishing mark of a competitor or of the designation of origin of competing products;
* Not present a good or service as an imitation or reproduction of a good or service whose trademark or trade name is protected.

 

Additionally, we note that whenever the comparison makes reference to a special offer, it must clearly and unequivocally state its term or, where applicable, that such special offer is subject to the availability of products or services, when this special offer has not yet started, the starting date of the period during which the special price or any other specific condition is applicable must also be indicated.

Please note that +the burden of proving the accuracy of comparative advertising lies with the advertiser+.

Furthermore, some products and services have specific advertising rules, such as is the case with medicines, financial services, energy and a few others. Consequently, some care should be taken when dealing with the marketing of these goods and services that have specific regulators.

 

*III.*             +*Fines/consequences for non-compliance with such legal requirements*+

In the case of illicit comparative advertising or advertising that, due to its object, form or purpose, entails or may entail risks to the health, safety, rights or interests legally protected of its addressees, minors or the public, the competent authority for the application of the fines provided for in the Portuguese law, upon proposal of the entities with competence for the supervision of advertising infractions, may order precautionary measures of suspension, cessation or prohibition of that advertising, regardless of guilt or proof of loss or real damage.

The above-mentioned fines are as follows:

* From

*1750 (euro) to 3750 (euro)* or from *3500 (euro) to 45 000 (euro),* depending on whether the offender is *a natural or legal person*.

* Negligence is always punishable.

Finally, any professional or competitor with a legitimate interest in combating misleading advertising and ensuring compliance with the provisions on comparative advertising may request the intervention of the Portuguese Directorate-General for Consumer Affairs.

It should also be noted that Portugal has a system of self-regulation in advertising matters. The self-regulation body is called Auto-Regulação Publicitária ([+https://auto-regulacaopublicitaria.pt/+|https://eur02.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fauto-regulacaopublicitaria.pt%2F&data=05%7C01%7Cvsandrade%40mlgts.pt%7C293e5e7692ee4782f3af08da76c49866%7C37dacaebcdcb4e5cbb53b1cb902cce84%7C0%7C0%7C637952883991302311%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJWIjoiMC4wLjAwMDAiLCJQIjoiV2luMzIiLCJBTiI6Ik1haWwiLCJXVCI6Mn0%3D%7C3000%7C%7C%7C&sdata=QcLGNen01Fd1lhw8qmUTlDHQHveOP7CGqtW4Kd29hLs%3D&reserved=0]).

Complaints may be filed with this entity and it will deliver very quick decisions regarding the lawfulness of advertising campaigns. The decisions are not binding to non-members but they carry a lot of weight and influence in Portugal and normally are highly publicized in the Portuguese media when the parties in question are well-known companies.

 

*IV.*             +*Any other legal considerations we must take into account.*+ 

We provide below some examples of comparative advertising that has been seen in Portugal.

Examples of comparative advertising:

Note: this comparative advertising is allowed if it is true. In this case, Lidl has even included the invoice as part of the campaign.

Note: whenever this price comparison corresponds to the truth and deals with comparable goods and services, comparative advertising is allowed (subject to the respect of the other conditions mentioned above also).

 

*V.*                +*Conclusion*+

In short, provided that Bolt Market follows the requirements mentioned above and puts together a truthful and fair campaign, it is possible to compare prices for certain products. This has been done in the recent past by supermarket chains such as Lidl and Intermarché.

Update received today from the CCPC:

Further to my email below, I have noted the information set out in your email of 22 July 2022.

Please appreciate that whilst the CCPC can give impartial information on the requirements of relevant legislation, we cannot provide legal advice.

Article 11(4) of the P2B Regulation states that platform providers must make the information on the functioning and effectiveness of their internal complaint-handling systems “easily available to the public”. While the appropriate means of providing the information will vary from platform to platform, a number of platforms publish this information in their terms and conditions, in a relevant section of their website (for example, the Legal section), or in a permanent footer.

In terms of the type of information that must be made available, Article 11(4) sets out that this must include the total number of complaints lodged, the main types of complaints, the average time period needed to process the complaints and aggregated information regarding the outcome of the complaints.

 Article 11(4) further states that the platform provider must verify the information at least annually, and should update the information if significant changes are needed.

I hope this information is useful to you and helps Bolt ensure compliance with Article 11 of the P2B Regulation.

There are different types of phone calls from one department to another. One is a cold transfer, meaning that a CS agent and a CS Safety agent do not speak with each other and a call gets transferred immediately. These phone calls should not happen in CS Safety. 
Another type of call is a warm transfer or a consultation call. A CS agent speaks with a CS Safety agent first and explains why a user is contacting Bolt. After this, a CS Safety agent determines if we need additional information from the user or not.

So, the request is just to explain that it has to be a consultation call. This way we will avoid cold transfers and it will also help users in the future. Imagine that we receive a “driver speeding” report and a passenger already told the story to the CS agent, so is there a point in telling the same story to the CS Safety agent? CS will still be able to do consultation calls and speak with the CS Safety agent, however, it doesn’t mean that CS Safety will proceed with the phone call with the passenger. This issue can work for regular cases when we have all the info (e.g driver speeding, driver swearing etc.), however, we will still take over calls regarding significant events or regular cases that are more serious (e.g. rider sexually touching themselves).

* The income from tips should be subject to income tax and corporation tax as usual at the level of the recipient (courier / fleet). 
* Normally, there should not be withholding tax issue in the case of tips on the basis that the tip is not paid directly by Bolt but by the Eater but maybe the Estonian tax authorities have a different view. Please comment in light of the latest discussions. 
* Where the Eater gets a refund (incl. the tip), where this cost falls on Bolt, the Estonian tax authorities may argue that the tip has been paid by Bolt and therefore subject to a withholding tax. The question is, where there are time differences in payment of the tip to the courier and a refund requested by the Eater, how the withholding tax obligation (if any) will be managed. 
* Similarly, in case of a refund, the cost of which is borne by Bolt, would it be non-taxable for Bolt for corporation tax purposes? As discussed in this Slack thread on #cskm-identity, the following details were confirmed:

* The user account deletion automation process flow won’t include the deletion of data on third-party platforms (such as Veriff and Onfido).
* This means that for removing the driving licence data, we’ll rely on the automatic driving licence verification data deletion rules in Veriff (9 months for Veriff, and for Onfido we switched the time from 3 to 9 months to match Veriff rules). 
* We can leave the Drive-specific process 🚙 [User requests to delete driving licence data|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/4404300054674] as it is.
* With the above details considered, *no further updates will be made* in the 🌍 [Rider or eater requests to delete account|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/360003841794--Rider-or-eater-requests-to-delete-account] to include instructions for deleting the user’s driving licence data.
** This means that if a user with a driving licence verified on their account will request their account to be deleted, they will face a DUPLICATED_USER error when they’ll try to verify their driving licence for the new account. For these cases, we have a process in place: 🚙 [User can’t pass driving licence verification|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/4408205581330#h_01G0BRGQXQB9C0WFE9QZKR9FRC]

Thank you for the ticket and apologies for the late response.

I agree with you that we should have some guidelines in the processes. However, with Safety cases, it is a bit tricky to have *clear* comp guidelines as most situations need to be evaluated case-by-case. As you also mentioned, it depends on what was the distance the user was able to travel with the vehicle, also did they have major injuries from the accident, if the rental was faulty, did it even cause an accident, etc. 

I’ve added a bullet-point about compensation to these two processes:

[User was injured or in an accident (rentals)|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360019440360]

* _Based on the severity of the event, consider refunding the trip_
** _Please note that this should be taken case-by-case. For example, if the rider was able to use the rental for some time and they didn't have major injuries, we shouldn't have to issue a refund. However, if the user could only use the rental for a very short time and/or had serious injuries, a refund might be justified._ 

[User reports a faulty scooter or e-bike|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/4901237473298]

* _Based on the severity of the event, consider refunding the trip_
** _Please note that this should be taken case-by-case. For example, if the rider was unable to use the rental (or could only use it for a very short time), we should issue a refund. If they got from point A to point B and only then discovered that the rental is faulty (and it didn't result in an accident), a refund wouldn't be justified._

----

In RH safety processes, I think we’ve already mentioned rider compensation. Some examples (I’ve understood OS only handles regular cases though):

* [Driver used hate speech or discriminated against the rider|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/4407126378642]
* [User reporting a vehicle accident or injury|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/4407393372050]
* [Driver was not alone in the vehicle|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/4407343213842]
* [Driver displays unprofessional behaviour|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/4408893605394]

I know it might be sometimes difficult for OS to determine whether a compensation is needed or not, but it really depends on the case as those safety cases are not as black-and-white as overcharge cases, for example, so agents have to use their own judgement and decide whether a refund (or some comp to BB in RH) is justified or not.

h3. How to take previous safety reports into account (Demerit Decay)?

Demerit Decay means that *older safety events should not be held against a user when considering their previous offences and consequential actions.* Safety events expire after a certain amount of time depending on the Risk Type if the user has not committed any more misconduct.

{color:#006644}When entering the number of previous incidents to the Occurrence field in the tool, count the number of previous reports together with the current one. {color}

* For *regular events*, it's 3 months. When checking for previous offences, only take into account offences {color:#006644}from the same Event Grouping{color} that took place within the last 3 months. 
* For *significant/unique events*, it's 1 year. When checking for previous offences, only take into account offences that took place within the last year. {color:#006644}We should count all precedents that highlight a pattern of behaviour, despite the Grouping.{color}
** {color:#006644}For example, the driver has two comments of inappropriate behaviour on their profile. We received a new report of sexual talk. ** Has to be sent from local authorities official address in written, on official letterhead, and include identity and authority of the officer
** The disclosure request is on an official law enforcement agency's letterhead as an attachment. The letterhead has certain identifying marks such as signature and stamp by the appropriate officer who is empowered by local law to represent the agency
** Thee personal data is requested in connection with the alleged crime (there is context and some details given of the investigation in hand)
** A precise description of the information requested, the reasoning of why information is requested, and how it relates to the investigation of the alleged crime
** Reference to applicable provisions of the relevant law (e.g domestic Data Protection Act) under which the agency is entitled to request the information. 
** Cites a provision for disclosure legitimising the request

Questions to solve and potential issues with recognizing a ticket’s process adherence:

* If process leaves space for agent’s decision/interpretation → is ticket adherent if the solution selected by agent was not the most efficient one?
* Do we include tickets that are more relevant to OPS tasks, i.e. without defined official processes?
* Is this binary or is it a scale?
** E.g. process was followed but incorrectly evaluated/process was followed but steps were skipped → do we still consider this adherent? This could technically bring more valuable data to Content team as it points to lower clarity of the process descriptions in KB
** Or maybe process was followed correctly but it was the incorrect process → article may be hard to identify?
* How do we work with this data when it comes to escalations? E.g. if original agent followed right procedure but the agent taking over did not
** Easiest - did last agent follow correct procedure? And it will go towards their performance
** The con is that if we do not cover all actors dealing with the ticket, we may miss on some incorrect solutions from earlier actors (perhaps ticket should not have been escalated at all)
* Should we change the way processes are written into a more binary solution with clear input criteria as opposed to something an agent can think about (something that CS product has considered as well)?

After the call with Content team:

* We should have _elements_ of processes, which will allow us to both look granularly into what happened but also can help us quantify the KPI → I’ll start with defining these elements now, but will most likely complete this once the final system is being defined
* Process creation is still an ongoing discussion in a sense, but in a longer term outlook, it’s likely they will become less adaptable to the opinion of the agent and hence will be easier to adapt to a possible automated system
* We can include OPS tasks, but just by getting a binary Y/N value to keep track of how many of them are done (since the evaluation is done on the ticket one way or another)

Potential elements:

* Is OPS process (Y/N
* Correct process followed (Y/N)
* Correct decisions/investigation followed (i.e. the path in the process was suitable for the situation) (maybe a score? No, partially, yes? Or some sort of a scale?)
* Final resolution (A scale)
* Escalation (was escalated → was escalated correctly? Should have been escalated?)



* Should also be separated between multiple agents if working on a ticket

Hi [~accountid:610d04058c15ca006f9988a6] our LT tax advisors have confirmed that, on the basis that the tip is voluntary for the customer (incl. the amount) and it does not comprise a part of the good/service price, it is not subject to VAT in Lithuania. 

The amount of the tip must be included on the invoice regardless of the tip not being subject to VAT. 

The tips received by couriers/fleets are likely subject to personal income tax / corporate income tax (as applicable) in Lithuania as part of their overall taxable income. It is recommended they seek tax advice from local advisers, as needed. 

Please also note that, as of 1 January 2023, Bolt as the reporting platform operator will have to collect and report the amount of tips (together with with any other fees) paid to couriers via our platform as part of the EU DAC7 reporting.

“\[*_Our advisor Sorainen_**:* the Law on VAT reads that any discounts not included in the unit price should be explicitly enlisted in the VAT invoice. Practically it follows that discounts need to be listed per each product if they are applied selectively, or differ per product, together taking into account VAT category (rate). Although, if a generalized discount is applied on the total purchase (let’s say 10% for everything) and the VAT category is the same (21% VAT applied on everything), indication of the overall discount applied on the total taxable value may be given and the charged applicable VAT indicated on the final amount.]

*To summarise:*

* Yes - discount has to be shown per product
* Yes - total discount needs to be shown per VAT rate
* If a general total discount is applied on the overall amount, discounts don’t need to be shown per product but nevertheless must be split per VAT rate if different rates apply.

Hi [~accountid:611b95f747d1df00762c6b63].

I generally agree with Tiiu - there is no VAT, and no withholding tax if the tips are paid from the eater to the courier and the eater does not revoke the tip in 32 hours.

The only issue we see from the tax side arises in this situation: _If the user/eater revokes tips after 32hrs, then we won’t reduce tips from the courier, but Bolt will compensate it for the Eater._

Here, as Tiiu said, the tax authorities have the grounds to say that since Bolt is covering the cost of this revoked tip then it can be deemed as our payment to the courier and we would need to withhold income tax on that (and also social tax under their current position). So we could either take this calculated risk of possible withholding (and social) tax or create a situation where Bolt would not cover the cost of the revoked tips. Happy to discuss if needed in the light of our current discussions with the tax authorities.

From corporation tax side we have arguments that this covering of the revoked tip costs serves our business interest of growing the platform so I think we should be good there.

According to the language course rules, Bolt is entitled to reclaim the course fee in full if the employee fails to pass or withdraws from the course.

Bolt can send a notice (example below) via email to the employee and reclaim the course fee. In the notice you can specify that there are two options how to reimburse the course fee to Bolt. Either settling the amount directly to Bolt bank account or give Bolt consent to deduct the amount from the next salary payment.

Once you have the consent from the employee, then the amount can be set-off against his/her salary. Please store the consent for the purposes of being able to submit evidence about it in case of disputes.

An example of the notice:

_Dear \[employee’s name],_

_In February 2022 Bolt offered voluntary Estonian language courses to which you participated/registered. According to the participating rules, the monetary cost to participate in the course was free, unless an employee fails to pass or voluntarily withdraws from the course. Here is the link to the rules, for you reference:_

_Unfortunately, you didn’t pass the course / did voluntarily withdraw from the course and therefore Bolt request to reimburse the course fee in the amount of 150 euros._

_There are two options for you to do that:_

# _Please settle the amount of 150 euros to the Bolt (specify the exact name of the legal entity, i.e. Bolt Operations OÜ or Bolt Technology OÜ) bank account no: XXXX, within 14 calendar days;_

_Or_  

2. _You can give Bolt a consent to set-off the amount of 150 euros against your next salary payment by responding to the email: I hereby give my consent to Bolt to deduct the amount of 150 euros from my salary to reimburse the cost of Estonian language course._

_Thank you in advance\!_

Let me know if you have any further questions.

3.6. Fikseeritud tasu. Teile võidakse pakkuda võimalust kasutada juhi pakutavat transporditeenust fikseeritud tasu eest. Fikseeritud tasu tehakse teile teatavaks Bolt’i rakenduse kaudu enne tellimuse kinnitamist. Fikseeritud tasu ei kohaldata, kui muudate sõidu ajal sihtkohta, sõit võtab liikluse või muude tegurite mõjul eeldatust oluliselt kauem aega või kui esinevad muud ootamatud asjaolud (nt kasutatakse marsruuti, kus kehtivad teemaksud).

Tarbijakaitsesse pöördunud kliendi sõiduhind muutus, kuna kliendi rakendusse esialgselt sisestatud sihtkoht muutus. Nagu on eelnevalt välja toodud, siis sellisel juhul muutub ka sõidu esialgne hind, sest kilometraaž ning kestus on eeldatust erinevad ning võib lisanduda ka teemaks.

Elektrooniline kokkuleppevedude süsteem peab muuhulgas:

* kuvama veo tellimisel sõitjale kokkuleppeveo tasu arvutamise meetodi. Siinkohal peab veo tellimisel, st siis, kui sõitja elektroonilise süsteemi abil alles veo teostajat alles valib, kuvama kõik tasud, mis veoga kaasnevad, et vältida ootamatuid lisatasusid. Seega peavad kajastatud olema sõidualustustasu, kilomeetri hind, seisutasu vm tasud, mis konkreetse veoga kaasnevad. Oluline on, et sõitjal oleks enne veo tellimist selge arusaam hinnakujundusest ning seeläbi teades veo pikkust, võimalik välja arutada ligikaudne veo lõpphind.



Kui kasutaja sisestab oma lõppsihtkoha, siis näidatakse talle sõidu lõplik maksumus, see broneeritakse tema maksevahenilt ning sellesse on hõlmatud nii aja-, kilometraaži-, kui ka muud tasud.
