Prepared rough copy of configuration from nginx (please check comments in the snippet), it fully works for few domains. At least was able to work with admin-panel/beehive via a locally deployed envoy without any issues.

This configuration covers: 

* Redirect http/https
* mTLS support 
* Multiple SSL support 
* Admin-panel routing logic
* Custom page for user without client certificate
* Fallback for okta auth  


Next steps → create epic for preparing infrastructure for it (ansible/terraform/s3/logging).

{noformat}static_resources:
  listeners:
  - name: http
    address:
      socket_address:
        address: 0.0.0.0
        port_value: 80
    #Enable listener on 80 to redirect to https.
    filter_chains:
      filters:
      - name: envoy.filters.network.http_connection_manager
        typed_config:
          "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.network.http_connection_manager.v3.HttpConnectionManager
          stat_prefix: ingress_http
          #TODO: Format logs for neseccary foramt
          access_log:
          - name: envoy.access_loggers.stdout
            typed_config:
              "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.access_loggers.stream.v3.StdoutAccessLog
          http_filters:
          - name: envoy.filters.http.router
            typed_config:
              "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.router.v3.Router
          route_config:
            name: redirect-to-https
            #All requests to all domain to 80 port redirect to 443 (via 301).
            virtual_hosts:
            - name: redirect-to-https
              domains: ["*"]
              routes:
              - match:
                  prefix: "/"
                redirect:
                   path_redirect: "/"
                   https_redirect: true
  - name: https
    address:
      socket_address:
        address: 0.0.0.0
        port_value: 443
    listener_filters:
    #TlsInspector needs filter by SNI (for multiple SSL certs).
    - name: "envoy.filters.listener.tls_inspector"
      typed_config:
        "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.listener.tls_inspector.v3.TlsInspector
    filter_chains:
    - filter_chain_match:
        #Filter by this name for SSL
        server_names:
          - "*.prelive.bolt.eu"
      filters:
      - name: envoy.filters.network.http_connection_manager
        typed_config:
          "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.network.http_connection_manager.v3.HttpConnectionManager
          stat_prefix: ingress_http
          #With Sanitize_set it pass cert details to upstreams. Without clarification of details it pass only hash.
          forward_client_cert_details: SANITIZE_SET
          #TODO: Format logs for neseccary format
          access_log:
          - name: envoy.access_loggers.stdout
            typed_config:
              "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.access_loggers.stream.v3.StdoutAccessLog
          http_filters:
          - name: envoy.filters.http.router
            typed_config:
              "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.router.v3.Router
          route_config:
            name: admin-panel-routes
            virtual_hosts:
              #match by domain
            - name: admin-panel.prelive.bolt.eu
              domains: ["admin-panel.prelive.bolt.eu"]
              request_headers_to_add:
                #TODO add CSP header (due to it's to massive for read)
                #Headers from nginx
                - header:
                    key: "X-XSS-Protection"
                    value: "1; mode=block"
                  append: true
                - header:
                    key: "X-Content-Type-Options"
                    value: "nosniff"
                  append: true
                - header:
                    key: "X-Permitted-Cross-Domain-Policies"
                    value: "none"
                  append: true
                - header:
                    key: "Strict-Transport-Security"
                    value: "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains"
                  append: true
                - header:
                    key: "expect-ct"
                    value: "max-age=604800, enforce"
                  append: true
              routes:
              - match:
                  #In nginx we use fallback after redirecting  via 302 to OKTA for auth, so added only this, doesn't find where else we use fallback, but mostly doesn't notice that it require somewhere.
                  safe_regex:
                    google_re2: {}
                    regex: "^(.*)login(.*)$"
                  headers:
                    #Match only requests which has this header, so if the client cert is not provided for this path envoy will return 404
                    - name: "x-forwarded-client-cert"
                      present_match: true
                route:
                  #rewrite HOST header to address of downstream.
                  auto_host_rewrite: true
                  regex_rewrite:
                    pattern:
                      google_re2: {}
                      regex: "^(.*)$"
                    #With admin-panel and beehive we s3 with file structure (s3://aws-s3/admin-panel.prelive|test.bolt.eu and so on. Envoy doesn't have any feature to place HOST value to path, that is why routing done per domain. The logic is that substitution value should be the save as vhost.
                    substitution: /admin-panel.prelive.bolt.eu/index.html
                  cluster: aws_s3
              #When admin-panel need to send request to nodejs service it add backend in the prefix, so we are matching requests to this path and in route forwarding it to envoy-internal.
              - match:
                  safe_regex:
                    google_re2: {}
                    regex: "^(.*)backend(.*)$"
                  headers:
                    - name: "x-forwarded-client-cert"
                      present_match: true
                route:
                  cluster: backend
                  auto_host_rewrite: true
                  regex_rewrite:
                    pattern:
                      google_re2: {}
                      regex: "/(backend)/(.*)"
                    #Example admin-panel/backend/service/ping -> envoy-internal/service/ping
                    substitution: /\2
              - match:
                  prefix: "/"
                  headers:
                    - name: "x-forwarded-client-cert"
                      present_match: true
                route:
                  auto_host_rewrite: true
                  regex_rewrite:
                    pattern:
                      google_re2: {}
                      regex: "^(.*)$"
                    substitution: /admin-panel.prelive.bolt.eu\1
                  cluster: aws_s3
              - match:
                  prefix: "/"
                #This match to root but without x-forwarded-client-cert needs to forwarding clients what doesn't pass certificate to another page. Right now beatiful html page is located on webserver, but in this case need to move it to S3 and route to it.
                route:
                  auto_host_rewrite: true
                  #TODO: Place html for 421 error from nginx repo to s3.
                  prefix_rewrite: "/bolt.eu/og-report-ebike.jpg"
                  cluster: aws_s3

            #Here tested second vhost
            - name: beehive.prelive.bolt.eu
              domains: ["beehive.prelive.bolt.eu"]
              request_headers_to_add:
                - header:
                    key: "X-Client-Certificate"
                    value: "accepted"
                  append: true
                - header:
                    key: "X-XSS-Protection"
                    value: "1; mode=block"
                  append: true
                - header:
                    key: "X-Content-Type-Options"
                    value: "nosniff"
                  append: true
                - header:
                    key: "X-Permitted-Cross-Domain-Policies"
                    value: "none"
                  append: true
                - header:
                    key: "Strict-Transport-Security"
                    value: "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains"
                  append: true
                - header:
                    key: "expect-ct"
                    value: "max-age=604800, enforce"
                  append: true
              routes:
              - match:
                  safe_regex:
                    google_re2: {}
                    regex: "^(.*)login(.*)$"
                  headers:
                    - name: "x-forwarded-client-cert"
                      present_match: true
                route:
                  auto_host_rewrite: true
                  regex_rewrite:
                    pattern:
                      google_re2: {}
                      regex: "^(.*)$"
                    substitution: /beehive.prelive.bolt.eu/index.html
                  cluster: aws_s3
              - match:
                  safe_regex:
                    google_re2: {}
                    regex: "^(.*)backend(.*)$"
                  headers:
                    - name: "x-forwarded-client-cert"
                      present_match: true
                route:
                  cluster: backend
                  auto_host_rewrite: true
                  regex_rewrite:
                    pattern:
                      google_re2: {}
                      regex: "/(backend)/(.*)"
                    substitution: /\2
              - match:
                  prefix: "/"
                  headers:
                    - name: "x-forwarded-client-cert"
                      present_match: true
                route:
                  auto_host_rewrite: true
                  regex_rewrite:
                    pattern:
                      google_re2: {}
                      regex: "^(.*)$"
                    substitution: /beehive.prelive.bolt.eu\1
                  cluster: aws_s3
              - match:
                  prefix: "/"
                route:
                  auto_host_rewrite: true
                  prefix_rewrite: "/bolt.eu/og-report-ebike.jpg"
                  cluster: aws_s3
      transport_socket:
        name: envoy.transport_sockets.tls
        typed_config:

!Screenshot 2022-08-12 at 11.32.23.png|width=1245,height=434!

If we compare January (0) to December (11,4), we get *11,4%*.

If we compare the whole period, we get *4,6%*.

I found a potential reason behind {{xinetd}}.
When Ansible copies the file to the instance it uses a handler to restart {{xinetd}}, however, if the playbook fails for any reason (like Nginx role), the handler isn't notified and {{xinetd}} doesn't restart.
I added this straight after copying the file to the instance:

{noformat}---
- name: Installing Availability Zone echo service (for discovery)
  ansible.builtin.copy:
    src: files/xinetd.d/availability-zone
    dest: /etc/xinetd.d/availability-zone
    owner: root
    mode: 0644
  notify: restart xinetd
  register: az_echo_service

- name: Restart xinetd
  ansible.builtin.service:
    name: xinetd
    state: restarted
  when:
    - az_echo_service.changed
{noformat}

*I suggest we address some of the vulnerabilities as part of the Account Management Epic:* [https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/BP-5891|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/BP-5891|smart-link] 

1 - *No Account Lockout*
We are going to change the account management allowing operators to have more control over their credentials, so let’s make sure we also add an account lockout if operators try to login with wrong passwords many times. 
1.1 - We will need to implement something similar to BP for a login with magic links in case that accounts are locked. 
1.2 - Accounts that do not have a valid e-mail address and end up locked will have to be handled by our CS, so we need to provide a way to unlock them on admin panel. Currently our CS can already change the password of the accounts, so it must be handled at the same view.

2 - *No Password Change Function*
Known issue, will be solved by the account management epic.

*Vulnerabilities that should be handled independently:*

1 - *Insecure Storage of JSON Web Token*
We are storing our tokens in the localStorage, and we must change it to use a HTTP-only cookie instead.
If we change it, the refresh_token won’t be available for the Ember APP, once it will not be available for JavaScript.
We need to double check the alternatives for it. We can follow the thread to see if there is already a way to solve it: [https://taxify.slack.com/archives/CGKURPTFS/p1626951967214700|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/CGKURPTFS/p1626951967214700|smart-link] 

2 - *Insufficient Rate Limiting Controls*
We don’t have any rate limiter on the authentication endpoints on the BE of the reseller app: [https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/c4638bf8f9765ee64ea6e23cf07382a34805b240/src/rides/marketplace/reseller/main/Bootstrap.ts#L377|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/c4638bf8f9765ee64ea6e23cf07382a34805b240/src/rides/marketplace/reseller/main/Bootstrap.ts#L377]

We can do something similar to what was done in BP and create a rate-limiter where the IP of the request is the key. That does not really solve all the possible attacks, once it is quite easy to get new IP addresses and it will not solve the issue if the attack is distributed.

Task for adding the rate limiter: [https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/BP-6005|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/BP-6005|smart-link] 

Another option would be to require a captcha validation, but if we do in this direction it can be handled as part of the account management epic. 
_We should also consider adding the 2fa as part of the account EPIC for operators that have a phone number attached to the account. It won’t solve the problem of brute force the password, but it will add extra security for accessing the portal._

3 - *Missing HTTP Security Headers*
Not much to add at this topic. Refer to the document and check the missing security headers.

These headers can be most likely added on CloudFront, but we have to keep in mind that RideBooker uses iframes and embeded objects and they can have problems with security headers. 

They are used by maps and by the seamless authentication with business portal (double check if the last one still exists)
